Tariq is the Editor-in-Chief of Space.com based out of our New York City office and joined the team in 2001, first as an intern and staff writer, and later as an editor. In 2000, Tariq became the city reporter for the Huntington Beach Independent, a weekly publication of the Los Angeles Times, covering local politics and events, crime, business and environmental issues. He left the Los Angeles Times in 2001 to study science journalism at New York University, where he earned a master's degree in 2002 from NYU's Science and Environmental Reporting Program (now the Science, Health and Environmental Reporting Program) under the direction of space reporter William Burrows.

Tariq first joined Space.com as an intern in September 2001 while also serving as a research assistant for nutrition writer Gary Taubes and writing freelance projects, where his work appeared in The Scientist and Laboratory Equipment Magazine. He became a full-time reporter covering spaceflight in 2004, with this first launch being NASA's STS-114 Return to Flight mission in July 2005.

Tariq is also an Eagle Scout (yes, he has the Space Exploration merit badge) and went to Space Camp four times as a kid and a fifth time as an adult. When not writing about space, you can find Tariq watching the latest Star Trek TV series, sci-fi movies and reading about hippos, his favorite animal. top.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
top.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. top.title: Kidnap: Police nab son over alleged N30m ransom demand from father
top.description: ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌‍⁠The Police Command in Ebonyi has arrested two suspects for allegedly staging a kidnapping and demanding a ransom of N30 million from the father of one of them. The suspects are Fortune Onuoha and his friend, Godspower Nkwo, popularly known as Hulk. The Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), SP Joshua Ukandu, disclosed this in a statement issued to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday in Abakaliki. Ukandu said the incident was reported on Oct. 31, 2026, at about 10:30 p.m., when Onuoha’s father contacted the Command’s Control Room to report that his son had been abducted from his hostel in Ikwo Local Government Area of the state. He said the complainant also reported receiving view-once videos and voice notes showing his son tied up, alongside demands for N30 million ransom by the purported kidnappers. According to him, the abductors threatened to kill the victim if the ransom was not paid. The PPRO said that following the report, the command deployed operatives to conduct an intelligence-driven investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged abduction and identify those responsible. He said sustained surveillance and discreet investigative efforts led to a breakthrough on Nov. 5, when police operatives arrested the two suspects as they emerged from the room where they had been hiding. Ukandu quoted the Commissioner of Police in the state, Mrs Urunwa Okafor, as warning members of the public against staging kidnappings or making false claims of abduction. According to the PPRO, the commissioner said such acts inflicted severe emotional trauma on parents, guardians, and loved ones while diverting valuable police resources from addressing genuine security threats. She stressed that staging kidnappings and making false abduction claims were criminal offenses punishable under the law. The police commissioner urged members of the public to shun criminal activities and embrace lawful means of addressing their challenges. top.description: USMNT Candidates - GOAL With Mauricio Pochettino heading to Manchester United, U.S. Soccer faces another defining hire. From ambitious global targets to familiar American faces, GOAL assesses who could lead the USMNT toward the 2030 World Cup. FAYETTEVILLE, Ga. -- Even with Mauricio Pochettino sitting beside him, U.S. Soccer CEO JT Batson began to speak about the future at the USMNT manager position. Pochettino doesn't officially depart for Manchester United until Wednesday, but that doesn't mean the process of replacing him hasn't already started. That process can be extensive. The USMNT doesn't have competitive fixtures until March, with next month's camp set to go ahead under Steve Cherundolo in a non-FIFA window. Given the four-month break between official games, U.S. Soccer can leave no stone unturned. And, according to Batson, they're already starting to turn over stones. "Our ambition is high," Batson said," and we believe that this is one of the great coaching jobs in the world. We have an experienced group of players. We've got a dynamic young pool of players...We publicly shared our ambition is to be in a position where we're winning major tournaments, including World Cups, and we want to make sure that we're attracting leaders who help us do just that. "We know from our experience that great leaders want to work with great people, and great leaders want to make an impact on things that matter. We think that we've proven that, at U.S. Soccer, we are a great place to work, and we're a great place to make legacy-defining impact." The coaching choice will define legacies, no doubt. Pochettino isn't an easy man to follow, and the road to the 2030 World Cup won't be a forgiving one. So who are the candidates that U.S. Soccer could target to lead the way? GOAL takes a look... Pep Guardiola U.S. Soccer has already reportedly made contact , and why wouldn't they? When the best coach of this century is on the market, you should probably give him a call, right? The good news is that the call isn't without reason. Guardiola has a famous affinity for New York and has been in contact with U.S. Soccer in the past. The timing has never been right, but might it be now? With Guardiola somewhat burnt out and having now conquered three of Europe's top five leagues, maybe? Manchester City's potential sanctions could play a part, too, in keeping Guardiola disillusioned with another European club project. If the Spain job were on the horizon, this would be a no. If Brazil were there, probably not, too. England? Maybe Guardiola would jump at that, but Thomas Tuchel is still there, at least for now. If Guardiola wants an international job, those would be his three dream opportunities, and none are particularly available. So, if Guardiola wants to work in something a little less stressful, the USMNT gig could be a good one. top.description: Substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto netted his first international goal with a late winner as Japan edged Brazil 3-2 in a thrilling friendly at the National Stadium in Singapore on Saturday. A brilliant brace by Vinicius Junior had erased a two-goal deficit after strikes by Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura put the Samurai Blue 2-0 up in the opening 19 minutes. But Sakamoto was in the right place to fire home after latching on to Kodai Sano’s deflected effort in stoppage time to give the Asian side a dramatic victory in front of 38,688 fans. In the first meeting between the teams since Brazil’s 2-1 win in the round of 32 at the World Cup in June, the Samurai Blue seized the early initiative with two goals in a torrid four-minute spell. On 15 minutes, a through ball by Ritsu Doan was picked up just inside the Brazilian half by Kubo who showed quick feet to cut inside Jair before firing a low effort past goalkeeper Pedro Morisco. Japan added another shortly afterwards after some fine work by Shuto Nakano, who broke down the right flank and centred for an unmarked Nakamura to calmly place a right-footed shot into the bottom corner of the net. Brazil responded with a magnificent goal by Vinicius in the 33rd minute. Zion Suzuki had made an excellent stop to deny Estevao when he bore down on goal, but the Japan goalkeeper could do little when the ball fell to Vinicius who found the top corner with a right-footed diagonal drive. Suzuki made good stops to deny Brazilian debutant Andre just before half-time and skipper Raphinha after the interval as Japan clung to their narrow lead. But the Selecao were not to be denied and Vinicius put them back on level terms in the 75th minute with another fine finish as he cut in from the left flank and launched a low right-footed effort that found the net off the right post. Brazil went close to grabbing the winner as substitute Endrick rocked the crossbar with a fierce effort and Joao Gomes sent a low shot narrowly wide. But in stoppage time, an effort by Kodai Sano took a fortunate bounce off a defender and fell nicely for Sakamoto to send the ball past Pedro Morisco. Brazil appealed for a foul in the build-up to the goal but VAR upheld the goal and Raphinha and manager Carlo Ancelotti were shown red card for their protests. top.description: Barcelona star speaks out against refereeing after red card vs Japan – “Cannot ignore” Raphinha’s international break will come to an early end as the forward was handed a red card in Brazil’s friendly match against Japan. It was the worst possible outing for Carlo Ancelotti’s men, who succumbed to a 3-2 defeat, with captain Raphinha and coach Carlo Ancelotti being shown a red late on . Speaking to the media after the game, the Barcelona star did not hold back in his assessment of the referee’s performance on the night. Raphinha on referees in Brazil vs Japan It was a frustrating evening for Raphinha. (Photo by Ashok Kumar/Getty Images) Operating as a right winger, Raphinha played 71 minutes before being replaced by Endrick, with Ancelotti opting for more freshness in attack. Having already endured a frustrating game, Raphinha’s evening got worse when he Japan score a 91st minute winner. Both Raphinha and Ancelotti reacted furiously from the bench, protesting a foul they believed had been made during the build-up. But both of them were shown straight red cards for their outbursts. Speaking to the media after the game, Raphinha offered an apology and took shots at the referee’s performance on the night. “I want to apologise for the red card, but it’s very complicated not to talk about the referee,” he said (h/t Mundo Deportivo ). “It’s difficult when you’re also playing against the referee. That complicates things a lot. I’m not saying we’re not to blame. We have a lot to improve and we will, but we cannot ignore today’s refereeing ,” he added. A good thing for Barcelona? Will Raphinha return early to Barcelona? (Photo by Koji Watanabe/Getty Images) Raphinha’s red card could be a boon for Barcelona, as he could very well be suspended for Brazil’s next friendly against Singapore. This means the forward will have the luxury of returning to Barcelona early, thus avoiding the risk of picking up a potential injury during the international break. This will be music to the ears for Hansi Flick, who has been quite fortunate with injuries piling up at a crucial juncture of the campaign. However, it is not yet confirmed whether or not Raphinha will indeed leave the Brazil camp early, and we will get more clarity in the coming hours.

top.description: Japan v Brazil - International Friendly - Getty Images Sport Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti has delivered a stinging assessment of the officiating following his side's dramatic 3-2 friendly defeat to Japan on Saturday. The veteran Italian tactician was sent to the stands during a heated conclusion to the match at the Singapore National Stadium, which saw the Selecao succumb to a late winner. Chaos in Singapore as Ancelotti sees red The atmosphere at the Singapore National Stadium turned sour in the final moments of Brazil’s clash with Japan . Despite Vinicius Junior finding the net twice, Brazil were unable to contain a clinical Japanese side. As Sakamoto found the net in added time to secure a famous victory for the Samurai Blue, the Brazilian bench erupted in protest. Amidst the heated scenes, referee Jansen Foo Chuan Hui brandished a red card to Carlo Ancelotti, leaving the former Real Madrid boss stunned on the touchline. Speaking in the aftermath of the defeat, Ancelotti was quick to clarify the official's reasoning for the dismissal. "He gave me the red card because he said I was not able to control the bench, and that all the players were on the field. That is the reason," the 67-year-old revealed, as quoted by Lance . Criticism of the officiating standards Ancelotti did not hold back in his assessment of the referee's performance, suggesting that the appointment for such a high-profile international fixture was a mistake. While he acknowledged the quality of the football on display, he felt the man in the middle lacked the necessary authority to manage the tension between two elite nations on the pitch. "A pity the result, because we don't like to lose the game, but we have to look at what we did well. There are many things. Some players who played for the first time, who showed good quality. For 70 minutes, the team was good. The result, obviously, is conditioned by the attitude of the referee, who did not blow the whistle," Ancelotti stated. He added, "But it's not his fault; it was a high-level match, and I think he didn't have the experience to manage this type of match." Japan's tactical discipline earns praise Ancelotti was also complimentary of the opposition, acknowledging that Japan’s rise in world football is no fluke. He noted their organizational strength and physical intensity as key factors that made life difficult for his stars, particularly in transition where the Samurai Blue were effective at nullifying Brazil's famous counter-attacking threat. "Japan is the same, the team is really well organized, with a lot of intensity, they fight a lot to avoid our counter-attack. And I am satisfied with the game we played, except for the beginning of the game, which was not good. After that, I think we reacted very well, we had the opportunity to equalize the game and try to win," Ancelotti concluded. top.description: After the first nine games of the season, the Chicago Bears are officially on bye with a chance to reset before their final eight games of the regular season and a playoff push in January. It goes without saying that defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons has been a stud for the Bears since Chicago’s blockbuster trade for him. He has also elevated multiple players around him on the defensive line, most notably his former college teammate, Montez Sweat, who finally looks like the Pro-Bowler the Bears traded for back in 2023. But there are numerous other players who need to improve for Chicago in the second half of the season, particularly on defense. Here are some more studs and duds from the first half of the Bears’ season, including running back D’Andre Swift, who leads the NFL in rushing touchdowns with 10. Stud: RB D’Andre Swift It is hard to find anyone on the Bears who has been more consistent through the first nine games of the season than running back D’Andre Swift. He leads the NFL in rushing touchdowns with 10, including two games this season with three rushing touchdowns. Swift actually has the fewest yards per attempt in a game this season of any year in his career, but he is also on track for his most carries in a season. Chicago has leaned on Swift to carry the run game throughout this entire season, especially with Kyle Monangai out since Week 5 and he has done a remarkable job. Swift is also currently on track to break the Bears’ franchise record for most rushing touchdowns in a season, which is currently 14. Dud: CB Tyrique Stevenson Chicago has dealt with injuries since training camp, especially in the secondary. Tyrique Stevenson briefly lost his starting job to rookie cornerback Malik Muhammad before Muhammad also got injured and the Bears had to put Stevenson back in the starting lineup. Defenses are picking on him because they know how poorly he is playing in coverage. Opposing quarterbacks have a 129.5 quarterback rating when targeting Stevenson so far this season and he has given up four touchdowns, including one on a blown coverage against the Seattle Seahawks. top.title: Nick Wright says what he has noticed about Aaron Rodgers is ‘going under the radar’
top.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers is heading into the most important game of the Pittsburgh Steelers’ 2026 season this weekend against the Cincinnati Bengals. The top spot in the AFC North is up for grabs, with both the Steelers and the Bengals going into the game with a 6-2 record. However, there are people questioning whether the Steelers stand a chance despite having already beaten Cincinnati earlier in the season. Rodgers is playing in his final season before calling time on his illustrious career, but his record of one touchdown and one interception over his last two games has not gone unnoticed. Heading into the game on Sunday, Nick Wright believes Rodgers is not showing enough to convince him the Steelers can win. Nick Wright thinks Aaron Rodgers’ performances are being swept under the rug The Steelers are on a four-game winning streak, but when comparing their points scored against the Bengals’, it is clear that Joe Burrow is operating at a different level from Rodgers and the Steelers. The Bengals have scored 240 points compared to the Steelers’ 180. “With Pittsburgh, because they’re 6-2, because Jaylen Warren’s been so good, and because the offense seems to be operating at a higher level, I think this has gone kind of under the radar: Aaron Rodgers, who we did not think was lighting the world on fire last year, is worse in everything this year,” Wright said on First Things First. “If you look at Rodgers’ numbers: the team scores less. He completes a far lower percentage of his passes. His yards per attempt, which was already near the bottom of the league, got worse. The touchdown-to-interception ratio, which was the one thing he kind of hung his hat on last year when it was 7.5 to 1, is down to 2 to 1. The passer rating has dipped by almost 10 points. In comparison, Burrow has thrown the same number of interceptions – including three against Tennessee – but he has also thrown 10 more touchdowns (23) than Rodgers. The game against the Bengals earlier in the season was one of Rodgers’ best performances of the season. nigeria.title: Kidnap: Police nab son over alleged N30m ransom demand from father
nigeria.description: ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌‍⁠The Police Command in Ebonyi has arrested two suspects for allegedly staging a kidnapping and demanding a ransom of N30 million from the father of one of them. The suspects are Fortune Onuoha and his friend, Godspower Nkwo, popularly known as Hulk. The Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), SP Joshua Ukandu, disclosed this in a statement issued to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday in Abakaliki. Ukandu said the incident was reported on Oct. 31, 2026, at about 10:30 p.m., when Onuoha’s father contacted the Command’s Control Room to report that his son had been abducted from his hostel in Ikwo Local Government Area of the state. He said the complainant also reported receiving view-once videos and voice notes showing his son tied up, alongside demands for N30 million ransom by the purported kidnappers. According to him, the abductors threatened to kill the victim if the ransom was not paid. The PPRO said that following the report, the command deployed operatives to conduct an intelligence-driven investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged abduction and identify those responsible. He said sustained surveillance and discreet investigative efforts led to a breakthrough on Nov. 5, when police operatives arrested the two suspects as they emerged from the room where they had been hiding. Ukandu quoted the Commissioner of Police in the state, Mrs Urunwa Okafor, as warning members of the public against staging kidnappings or making false claims of abduction. According to the PPRO, the commissioner said such acts inflicted severe emotional trauma on parents, guardians, and loved ones while diverting valuable police resources from addressing genuine security threats. She stressed that staging kidnappings and making false abduction claims were criminal offenses punishable under the law. The police commissioner urged members of the public to shun criminal activities and embrace lawful means of addressing their challenges. nigeria.title: Otti, Ajaero, others pay tributes to late NLC scribe, Ugboaja
nigeria.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — It was a night of tears, fond memories and glowing tributes on Friday as labour leaders, government officials, family members and associates gathered in Umuahia to celebrate the life and legacy of the late Secretary-General of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Comrade Emmanuel Okechukwu Ugboaja. Ugboaja, who hailed from Nkpa in Bende Local Government Area of Abia State, died at the age of 60. At the Night of Tributes organised by the Abia State Government at the International Conference Centre, Umuahia, speakers took turns to recount the late labour leader’s contributions to workers’ welfare, organised labour and humanity, describing his death as an irreparable loss. Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, who led the tributes, described Ugboaja’s death as painful, but said his contributions to the labour movement and society would remain an enduring legacy. Otti particularly celebrated his emergence as the first and only indigene of Abia State to occupy the position of NLC Secretary-General among the five individuals who had held the office. “Out of the five Secretaries-General of the Nigeria Labour Congress, Comrade Emmanuel Ugboaja was the only one from Abia State. “He was the first NLC Secretary-General from our State, and that is a significant achievement,” the governor said. Reflecting on the meaning of life, Otti said a person’s worth was not measured by the number of years spent on earth but by the positive impact made and the legacies left behind. He expressed confidence that the late Ugboaja had successfully fulfilled his earthly assignment, urging his family not to surrender to despair but to draw strength from the Christian hope of resurrection. “From everything we have heard about him today, we have no doubt that Comrade Emmanuel Ugboaja finished his race here on earth. There are no mistakes with God. “We urge the family not to mourn like those without hope. Our prayer is that on the resurrection morning, when the trumpet shall sound, Comrade Emmanuel Ugboaja will be among those who will rise to eternal life,” Otti said. nigeria.title: Clashes between gangs, vigilantes kill over 50 in Zamfara – Report
nigeria.description: Clashes between criminal gangs and local vigilantes have left more than 50 people dead in northwestern Nigeria’s Zamfara state, residents told AFP Saturday. Zamfara is one of several states in northwest and central Nigeria terrorised by kidnapping-for-ransom and cattle-rustling gangs who raid villages, kill and abduct residents as well as looting homes before burning them. Locals call the gangs bandits. Vigilantes from Zoma village in Bukkuyum district ambushed the bandits who were passing through the village on Thursday after kidnapping several people from nearby Gummi district, the sources said. “We were alerted that the bandits were heading our way, so our vigilantes laid in wait for the bandits and engaged them in a fierce gunfight,” said a traditional village chief who asked not to be identified for personal safety. “Our vigilantes killed 44 of the bandits … we also lost nine vigilantes in the fight,” said the chief, adding that a notorious bandit commander called Jijji, who had led the kidnapping, was also killed in the fight. – Call for weapons – News of bandit attacks in remote areas is usually slow to emerge due to poor telecommunications and distance. A Zamfara state police spokesman contacted by AFP said the force had yet to receive details about the clashes. Zoma residents Kabiru Tafida and Basiru Buhari reached by AFP gave the same account of the clashes and toll. “We call on the authorities to provide our vigilantes with guns and ammunition to fight these bandits who use sophisticated weapons,” Buhari said. Banditry in Africa’s most populous country traces its roots to conflicts between herders and farmers over access to limited land and water, made worse by climate change and population growth. Out of the violence emerged powerful gangs, largely composed of Fulani herders — and a kidnapping economy, while at times forging alliances with jihadists. In Zamfara’s neighbouring state Katsina, a bandit leader recently told AFP that “years of injustices” drove him and other cattle herders into banditry. He spoke during a rare interview which came during the reporting of an article for The New York Review of Books, co-authored by an American academic and writer Helen Epstein and an AFP northern Nigeria reporter. The Nigerian military routinely refers to bandits as “terrorists”, and runs a dedicated military campaign in the northwest to combat them. Worsening insecurity and the high cost of living have become major issues in the ongoing presidential campaign, as Bola Tinubu runs for a second term in January polls. nigeria.title: ‘Truly beautiful’ to make football return, says Ronaldinho
nigeria.description: Brazilian great Ronaldinho says it will be “truly beautiful” to make his return to the pitch on Sunday, 11 years after retirement, when he plays for Italian third-tier side Ravenna. The 46-year-old, who last played for Fluminense in 2015, will start for Ravenna in their local derby against Forli. “I want to have a great day. I’m happy to be here for the start of this wonderful story,” Ronaldinho told Sky Sports on Friday. “The president dreams of something big for Ravenna, and being a part of it makes me happy.” Ravenna president Ignazio Cipriani has said his goal is to take the club to Serie A for the first time in their history. The team’s Stadio Bruno Benelli, which usually holds 5,000 fans, is sold out, with a 1,800-capacity temporary stand — dubbed “R10” — also erected for the occasion. Ravenna, who have not even played in Serie B since 2008, are second in their group in Serie C, six points behind leaders Spezia. “Returning to the pitch after so much time is truly beautiful — I’m here to experience a special moment in my life,” added Ronaldinho. “It’s been a few years since I stopped playing — I’ve won everything I ever dreamed of. “Now I’m 46, and I’ve experienced everything there is to experience in football. This is a completely different kind of opportunity. I want to be part of the dream held by my friends who work for Ravenna.” The 2005 Ballon d’Or winner will be hoping to score his 300th career goal, over a decade after he netted his 299th. The former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain star has even spent time in a Paraguayan prison since, after attempting to enter the country on a false passport, but did star in a prison futsal match. The move to Ravenna is widely regarded as a marketing stunt, but one Cipriani hopes can help kickstart his Serie A dream. “The long-term goal is to get Ravenna promoted to Serie A,” insisted the club president. The festival, which attracts more than 25,000 attendees across its programme days, has become one of the most anticipated events on Lagos’s cultural calendar. This year’s festival is themed “The Masks We Wear”, anchored by the statement “The Stage Is Everywhere.” The theme explores the different roles and identities people assume in everyday life, while inviting audiences to consider how theatre extends beyond the traditional stage. LITF 2026 brings an international dimension to Lagos, featuring artists and productions from Kenya, Canada and Brazil alongside a diverse Nigerian programme. This will be followed by Embassy Nights on November 10 and 11, celebrating international cultural exchange among diplomatic representatives, artists and creative industry leaders. The programme culminates in an Opening Night Gala on November 13, ahead of the main festival weekend at MUSON Centre on November 14 and 15. LITF 2026 is supported by the Lagos State Government, LekOil, Pillar Oil, Afrexim and Amstel , alongside its growing network of international and cultural partners. Founder of LITF, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “The Masks We Wear is a theme that speaks to all of us. entertainment.description: Shirley U. Emehelu, New Jersey’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State. Photo Credit: Official Site of New Jersey A Nigerian-born legal leader has made history in New Jersey. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has officially appointed Nigerian-American Shirley U . Emehelu as the state’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State . Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. In that role, she directly counselled the Attorney General, coordinated oversight for more than 500 attorneys within the Division of Law—New Jersey’s largest legal office—and directed civil defence and enforcement matters across civil rights, environmental protection, labour and consumer protections, data privacy, and firearms safety. New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Shirley U. Emehelu, part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Photo Credit: Shirley U. Emehelu/LinkedIn Earlier in her career, Emehelu spent nine years at the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Jersey, serving as Chief of Asset Recovery and Anti-Money Laundering, where she prosecuted complex financial fraud cases and oversaw statewide asset forfeiture and victim restitution programmes. She also practised in the private sector as a member of the White-Collar Criminal Defense and Government Investigations Group at CSG Law, co-leading the firm’s Banking and Finance Group, after clerking for the Honourable James R.Spencer in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia. There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. sports.description: USMNT Candidates - GOAL With Mauricio Pochettino heading to Manchester United, U.S. Soccer faces another defining hire. From ambitious global targets to familiar American faces, GOAL assesses who could lead the USMNT toward the 2030 World Cup. FAYETTEVILLE, Ga. -- Even with Mauricio Pochettino sitting beside him, U.S. Soccer CEO JT Batson began to speak about the future at the USMNT manager position. Pochettino doesn't officially depart for Manchester United until Wednesday, but that doesn't mean the process of replacing him hasn't already started. That process can be extensive. The USMNT doesn't have competitive fixtures until March, with next month's camp set to go ahead under Steve Cherundolo in a non-FIFA window. Given the four-month break between official games, U.S. Soccer can leave no stone unturned. And, according to Batson, they're already starting to turn over stones. "Our ambition is high," Batson said," and we believe that this is one of the great coaching jobs in the world. We have an experienced group of players. We've got a dynamic young pool of players...We publicly shared our ambition is to be in a position where we're winning major tournaments, including World Cups, and we want to make sure that we're attracting leaders who help us do just that. "We know from our experience that great leaders want to work with great people, and great leaders want to make an impact on things that matter. We think that we've proven that, at U.S. Soccer, we are a great place to work, and we're a great place to make legacy-defining impact." The coaching choice will define legacies, no doubt. Pochettino isn't an easy man to follow, and the road to the 2030 World Cup won't be a forgiving one. So who are the candidates that U.S. Soccer could target to lead the way? GOAL takes a look... Pep Guardiola U.S. Soccer has already reportedly made contact , and why wouldn't they? When the best coach of this century is on the market, you should probably give him a call, right? The good news is that the call isn't without reason. Guardiola has a famous affinity for New York and has been in contact with U.S. Soccer in the past. The timing has never been right, but might it be now? With Guardiola somewhat burnt out and having now conquered three of Europe's top five leagues, maybe? Manchester City's potential sanctions could play a part, too, in keeping Guardiola disillusioned with another European club project. If the Spain job were on the horizon, this would be a no. If Brazil were there, probably not, too. England? Maybe Guardiola would jump at that, but Thomas Tuchel is still there, at least for now. If Guardiola wants an international job, those would be his three dream opportunities, and none are particularly available. So, if Guardiola wants to work in something a little less stressful, the USMNT gig could be a good one. Even so, though, he'll have his choice of suitors, which means you can still probably file this under the "unlikely" category. Thierry Henr

The sporting director oversaw the highly lucrative departures of Randal Kolo Muani and Willian Pacho, bringing enormous transfer fees into Frankfurt. He also played a vital role in the successful recruitment and rapid development of Egyptian forward Omar Marmoush. Milan are desperate to tap into this proven expertise. The club hierarchy wants a strong figurehead capable of mastering both global player recruitment and high-value outbound sales. sports.title: Question of the Day: How far do Bears have to go for you to be satisfied?
sports.description: Mike Ditka, Chicago Bears' coach, holds a press conference with the Vince Lombardi Trophy firmly in his grasp after his team wins the Super Bowl. (Photo by Bettmann Archive/Getty Images) The Chicago Bears have hit the bye at 7-2 and are sitting in first place of the gauntlet NFC North. The Bears have a tough second-half schedule but certainly appear to be headed to the playoffs for the second consecutive year. Last season, the Bears won the division, won their first playoff game in 15 years, and they were an eyelash away from reaching the NFC Championship Game. I think 99% of Bears fans, after the sting of the Rams loss wore off, were very pleased with the results of the 2025 season, even if they lost the last game they played. This year, at approximately the midway point in the season, the Bears are at or near the top of everyone’s list of a true Super Bowl contender. With more success comes more expectations. How far do Bears have to go for you to be satisfied with their season? I think as fans, when the team is building something, we want to see them improve upon the previous season. Since there were only four teams that had more postseason success than Chicago, there isn’t a ton of room to improve. That being said, I think Bears fans and NFL media around the country expect the Bears to be better than they were in 2025. Answer: I think the first obvious step is that for any level of satisfaction to be reached, the Bears have to be one of the last four remaining teams in the NFL. That’s a lofty thing to say, but I think it’s fair. I think if the Bears make the playoffs but lose in the Wild Card or Divisional round, there will be plenty of disappointment with the fan base. Yes, fans will be excited that the Bears made the playoffs in back-to-back seasons for the first time since 2005 and 2006, but that won’t be good enough. Even if the Bears win a playoff game in back-to-back seasons, it’ll be the first time they’ve done that since 1984 and 1985, but even then, that won’t be good enough. I think for some fans, reaching the NFC Championship Game will be enough. If the San Francisco 49ers are the 1 seed and the Bears go on the road and lose in that game, there will be a certain level of satisfaction, but I still don’t think that’s enough. I think the Bears need to reach the Super Bowl for me to walk away feeling excited without too much disappointment. Obviously, I want them to win, but if Josh Allen climbs the mountaintop and beats the Bears and wins the Super Bowl, am I going to be freaking out? No, I just think the Bears will be ready to take the next step in 2027. What say you, Bears fans? How far do the Bears have to go this year for you to be content with their season? Is it Super Bowl or bust, like it is for Bill Zimmerman? Is it the Lombardi Trophy? Or is a lower level of success good enough for you? Sound off in the comments below!

technology.title: James Webb telescope finds ice older than the star it orbits
technology.description: Beta Pictoris is a young star, roughly 20 million years old, and located about 64 light-years away from Earth. It is surrounded by a vast disk of dust and rubble where planets are still forming—astronomers have already found three. In a new Science study, a team led by Sarah Betti, an astronomer at the Space Telescope Science Institute in Baltimore, used the James Webb Space Telescope to look for ice in this disk. Researchers found both water and carbon dioxide ice. The water ice is glassy rather than crystalline, and it is mixed with carbon dioxide in roughly the same proportions we see in comets of our own Solar System. This suggests ingredients necessary to form water-rich worlds might be common around young stars. The missing ice Beta Pictoris is one of the best studied stars in the sky. Its disk was among the first ever imaged, back in 1984, and we see it almost exactly edge-on, which makes it a natural laboratory for studying how planetary systems grow. It's what astronomers call a debris disk, where the dust is constantly replenished by collisions among comets and planetesimals, small bodies that are the building blocks of planets. technology.title: Big Tech takes a beating as online safety experts accuse companies of doing bare minimum
technology.description: Technology companies are doing just enough to show a degree of compliance with the UK's Online Safety Act, but are failing to meet the needs of the individuals and young victims the legislation exists to protect, experts say. A panel of online safety pros assembled before Parliament's Communications and Digital Committee on Tuesday, taking aim at the likes of Google, Microsoft, Meta, and ByteDance for failing to act on important matters. Clare McGlynn, professor of law at Durham University and expert on violence against women and girls (VAWG), was especially critical of major search engine providers for their inconsistent downranking of harmful content search terms. "Rape porn," for example, is correctly downranked and no user sees any relevant links until the tenth page of results, although adjacent terms such as "unwilling porn" can be found as early as the third page, McGlynn said. "I just think if someone spent a little more time thinking 'I really want to minimize the risk of this material appearing,' I would take a systematic approach," she told the committee. "I would downrank 'unwilling' and 'unwanted,' and I would downrank 'asleep porn' as well… because it just means that it's easily findable. "So, they don't rank some of them, but just not systematically or wholly consistently." McGlynn went on to say that during her own research, "force porn" was rightly downranked heavily, although terms as similar as "forced porn" were not. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972. science.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
science.description: null This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed. In more recent years, most notably 1999 , 2001 and 2002 , lesser Leonid displays of up to "only" a few thousand meteors per hour took place. Unfortunately, that's not likely to be the case this year. In fact, comparatively speaking, this is going to be a lean year for the Leonids chiefly because of the expected lack of any significant activity. Although the Leonids are one of the most famous of all the annual meteor displays, this year they're not likely to be very productive. It's probable they are going to be rather weak and there probably will be long stretches when not a single Leonid will be seen. I'll explain why in a moment. First, let's find out about this shower's lineage. What causes the Leonids? The Leonids are so named because the shower's radiant point, from where the meteors seem to fan out, is located within the constellation of Leo the Lion, from the backward question mark pattern of stars known as " The Sickle." The meteors are caused by the Tempel-Tuttle comet , which sweeps through the inner solar system every 33⅓ years. Each time the comet passes closest to the sun it leaves a "river of rubble" in its wake: a dense trail of dusty debris. A meteor storm becomes possible if the Earth were to score a direct hit on a fresh dust trail ejected by the comet over the past several centuries. The "lion's share" (no pun intended) of comet dust can be found just ahead and trailing behind Tempel-Tuttle. That comet last swept through the inner solar system in 1998. That's why spectacular meteor showers were seen in 1999, 2001 and 2002, with declining numbers thereafter. The most famous depiction of the 1833 Leonids, actually produced in 1888 for the Adventist book Bible Readings for the Home Circle . The engraving is by Adolf Vollmy based upon an original painting by the Swiss artist Karl Jauslin, that is in turn based on a first-person account of the 1833 storm by a minister, Joseph Harvey Waggoner on his way from Florida to New Orleans. science.title: 100 launches! Rocket Lab sends Earth-observing satellite to orbit on milestone mission (photos)
science.description: null Rocket Lab just hit the century mark. An Electron rocket topped with a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite lifted off from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site on Saturday (Nov. 14) at 12:30 a.m. EST (0530 GMT; 6:30 p.m. local New Zealand time). The mission, which Rocket Lab called "The Mountain God Rises," was a big one: It marked the 100th launch to date for the California-based company. The first stage of Rocket Lab's Electron rocket falls back to Earth during "The Mountain God Rises" mission on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) Rocket Lab launched for the first time in May 2017, sending the brand-new Electron up on a test flight from New Zealand. That effort failed, but Electron bounced back on its second-ever liftoff, delivering several cubesats to low Earth orbit (LEO) in January 2018. In the years since, the 59-foot-tall (18 meters) Electron has become one of the most prolific and reliable rockets in the world, carrying small payloads to the final frontier for a variety of customers. And it hit the century mark on Saturday in record-breaking fashion: No commercially developed rocket has gotten there faster, not even SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9 , according to Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck. "It's an unprecedented milestone for a commercial small-lift orbital rocket, and a threshold rarely crossed in modern spaceflight," Beck said on Monday (Nov. 9), during Rocket Lab's third-quarter earnings call with investors. "But what matters most to us and our customers is that we have achieved a 96% reliability rate across 99 launches." Electron met the moment in style on Saturday morning, thanks to some fancy livery. "Black rocket 🤝 Golden milestone. Electron is all dressed up for launch 100," Rocket Lab said via X on Tuesday (Nov. 10), in a post that shared a photo of the specially painted first stage. Not all of Rocket Lab's missions have gone orbital, it should be noted: A suborbital variant of Electron known as HASTE , which customers use to test technologies in a hypersonic flight environment, has nine missions under its belt to date. The Electron rocket that flew Rocket Lab's 100th mission sported some special livery. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) "The Mountain God Rises" was Rocket Lab's 11th launch to date for the Tokyo-based company iQPS, which is building a constellation of three dozen synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites in LEO. And all went to plan on the mission: Electron's upper "kick stage" deployed a single iQPS spacecraft 357 miles (575 kilometers) above Earth. SAR satellites can see through cloud cover and image our planet at night as well as during the day, offering key advantages over spacecraft that are optimized to view in optical wavelengths. science.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

In many of the biggest science fiction franchises, conversing with alien races is an absolute doddle. In " Star Trek ", universal translators come as standard, while C-3PO has spent the last 49 years reminding everyone in "Star Wars" that he's fluent in over six million forms of communication. But in "Arrival" — which was released 10 years ago in November 2016 — making first contact proves to be rather more challenging than maintaining your Duolingo streak. In fact, working out how to establish a dialogue with extraterrestrial visitors becomes the whole point of this powerful and heartbreaking story, as the fate of planet Earth hinges on the interpretation of a single noun. The film's journey to the big screen began when a screenwriter best known for his work on horror franchises such as "Final Destination", "A Nightmare on Elm Street" and "The Thing" read a short story in an online magazine. Eric Heisserer was so impressed by Ted Chiang's "Understand" that he bought himself a collection of the author's short stories. science.title: California's brand-new Air & Space Center, home of the space shuttle Endeavour, opens today
science.description: null LOS ANGELES — The California Science Center officially opened its brand-new Samuel Oschin Air & Space Center to the public today (Nov. 13). After more than three decades in development, folks can finally visit the Los Angeles science museum's massive new wing. For most of us, the biggest draw is its centerpiece: the retired space shuttle Endeavour , sitting upright in launch position, towering at nearly 200 feet (61 meters) tall. "It just takes your breath away when you see that reveal and the doors open and you get to look at it for the first time. It's just — it's overwhelming," former NASA astronaut Garrett Reisman told Space.com during a visit to the museum. Reisman flew on two space shuttle missions during his astronaut career, the first of which was on Endeavour. The space shuttle Endeavour. (Image credit: Olivia Hemaratanatorn/Future) "There are people that come from all over the world, and when they come to Los Angeles, they're going to have the opportunity to see it, too," Reisman added. "The exposure it's going to have is just a force multiplier. There are so many people that can have that opportunity to bring their kids here and show them [the shuttle] and have that experience." Entering into this exhibit is an experience in and of itself, as I can personally attest; I was among of group of reporters who got a sneak peek at the new wing on Oct. 28. A video presentation ends in a dramatic reveal: Visitors walk into a space where the enormous shuttle, which flew 25 missions to Earth orbit from 1992 to 2011, feels truly larger than life. The new Endeavour exhibit features a replica launch tower, from which you can look down at the shuttle. (Image credit: Future) There are a number of interactive exhibits around the base of Endeavour, which you can slide down to (though, of course, you can also take the elevator or stairs). From a shuttle landing simulator to a replica of a shuttle cockpit that you can sit in, to shuttle tires and space tech from across decades of spaceflight history, there's an incredible variety of space artifacts to both observe and interact with. As for Endeavour itself: It is open, so you can peer inside to see the robotic arm tucked away among a myriad of handles, straps and electronic gear inside. And you can see the shuttle from underneath all the way to the top. A replica of the space shuttle Endeavour's flight deck. (Image credit: Olivia Hemaratanatorn/Future) You can lie on the floor underneath the shuttle's engines, for example, and then take an elevator up the launch tower to come face-to-face with Endeavour's nose. There's even a transparent floor at the top that allows you to stand above the shuttle (though if you have a fear of heights, this might not be for you). science.title: Think you have good eyesight? Try counting the stars in the Pleiades tonight
science.description: null Every autumn, I conduct an eyesight test that no reputable optometrist would understand. I go outside, find the Pleiades and count how many stars I can see. Usually I start confidently. One, two, three, four, five. Then things become contentious. Is that another star? Did I actually see it, or did I decide I ought to see it because I know it's there? I look away, look back and begin again. This is not, I should emphasize, a meaningful test of eye health. What it tests, rather, is how badly I've prepared for looking at the night sky. The Pleiades sit roughly 444 light-years away in Taurus and are right now becoming extremely convenient in the evening sky. You don't need a telescope to find them. You don't even need binoculars. In fact, you're likely to catch their collective brightness in your peripheral vision every time you go outside and look up. But every November the Pleiades remind me that naked-eye observing isn't as simple as opening the back door and looking up. How many Pleiades I can see can change depending on what I do during the next 10 minutes. What's happening and when to look You can easily see the Pleiades as a bright misty patch in your peripheral vision during winter. (Image credit: Haitong Yu via Getty Images) The Pleiades, also known as Messier 45 (M45) or the "Seven Sisters," are an open star cluster in Taurus. They're one of the closest clusters to the solar system and some of the youngest stars you can see with the naked eye — just 100 million years old. They're basically newborns. In mid-November, they rise in the east in the early evening and climb higher as the night progresses, making this an excellent time to get acquainted with them. Look east after dark for a tiny, compact group of stars. If you know Orion, which rises later, the Pleiades are above and to the right of it from mid-northern latitudes. Nearby you'll also find orange Aldebaran and the much broader V-shaped Hyades cluster. The Hyades are closer to the sun , but their stars are about 625 million years old. The name "Seven Sisters" creates an immediate observational trap: people assume they're supposed to see seven stars. That's not necessarily true. In fact, six is a common naked-eye result under decently dark conditions (note that the shape of the six brightest is like a mini Big Dipper /Plough), while people with sharp eyesight under darker skies may see more. The cluster itself contains about 1,000 stars. The number you personally distinguish depends on eyesight, sky brightness, atmospheric conditions and how well your eyes have adapted to darkness. That makes M45 much more interesting to me than a simple tick-box target. So tonight, don't just find the Pleiades — count them. science.title: 'Martian Isolation' is an upcoming sci-fi survival horror game that looks like 'The Martian' and 'Event Horizon' had a horrific child
science.description: null "Martian Isolation" is an upcoming single-player, first-person survival horror game that's just been revealed with a suitably creepy launch trailer. And yes, it does look an awful lot like " The Martian ," doesn't it? There's a lot of survival gameplay on display here that mirrors Mark Watney's tale of survival on the Red Planet, as your stranded protagonist is forced to explore the Martian surface to acquire resources, grow plants, and repair their base. That comparison to Andy Weir's sci-fi masterpiece does fall away as you get further into the trailer, though, when the horror part of the game's description comes into play: Flickering lights, creepy figures stalking the halls of your Martian habitat, and blood dripping from the walls. Oh yeah, that's some good creepy sci-fi horror right there. It's giving " Event Horizon ", and that's always getting a thumbs-up from me. There's no release date scheduled at this time, with the 'Martian Isolation' Steam page simply listing it as "coming soon," though the YouTube trailer description does say it "will be available on Steam in 2027". You can't pre-order yet, but if this looks like your jam, you can add it to your wishlist. Beyond that, we know shockingly little about this title. It's the debut game from Golden Milestone Studio, but there's very little information out there beyond a name. The latest blog post on the game's Steam page says that they're a "small team," but what we've seen so far is encouraging. There seems to be a pronounced split between the survival and horror elements of the game along the day/night cycle. Daytime sees you exploring the Martian surface, smashing rocks, cleaning solar panels, and doing sick jumps on a quad bike. The psychological torment only begins once the sun goes down (they mostly come out at night … mostly), as your character starts encountering cosmic horrors and weird naked zombie men. Mars rover, nice. Golden Milestone Studio Spacesuits, check. Golden Milestone Studio Crafting, of course. Golden Milestone Studio OH SWEET JESUS! Get it away, get it away. Golden Milestone Studio OK, we're good. Mining, cool. Golden Milestone Studio Riding a quad bike on Mars, yes please. Golden Milestone Studio Growing potatoes on Mars, just like that guy in the movie. Golden Milestone Studio Opening a box with power tools, seems excessive but sure. Golden Milestone Studio NOPE! Nope, nope, nope, I'm out! Golden Milestone Studio Are they hallucinations, or is there some malevolent presence hiding in the blood-red sands of Mars ? I'm always looking for new ways to shatter my psyche and possibly soil my pants, so I'll be keeping a close eye on this one. In the meantime, I do need to get back and finish " Routine ." I left my character hiding under a desk months ago, and I haven't been brave enough to go back. As Mama always said, you can't have any Martian horror until you finish your lunar horror first.

science.title: Astronomers trace mystery radio signals back to cosmic odd couple of white dwarf and sun-like star
science.description: null Astronomers have traced a mysterious radio signal back to a cosmic odd couple comprised of a dead star, a white dwarf, and its stellar companion, a sun-like star. The white dwarf in the newly discovered system, designated GPM J071507−114153 and located around 5,000 light-years away, spins once every eight minutes, sending out radio pulses. These radio pulses have been seen from binary systems with smaller and cooler red dwarf stars before, but rarely from a system like GPM J071507−114153. GPM J071507−114153 belongs to a class of celestial objects called long-period transients (LPTs) known to produce radio signals that switch on and off over intervals of minutes or hours. Around a dozen LPTs have been detected since the team behind this research found the first in 2021. Several previously discovered LPT systems contain a white dwarf and a companion star, but it has been unclear which of the two stars was generating the radio pulses. That means the discovery of GPM J071507−114153 and finding that the pulses come from close to the white dwarf could be a significant step toward understanding the nature of LPTs. The unusual system consists of a small and highly energetic white dwarf pulsar, orbiting a much larger star similar to our sun. (Image credit: ICRAR) "This is the first time the pulses are clear enough to see the white dwarf moving in its orbit around its companion," team leader and commissioning scientist with the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKA), Sam McSweeney, said in a statement . "So we know that the pulsations are coming from a region close to the white dwarf, or possibly even from the white dwarf itself." The pulses seen by the team also allowed them to detect stellar flares erupting on the sun-like star. "As a bonus, we also saw the white dwarf moving behind a region with a strong magnetic field, most likely a 'stellar prominence,' which is a large loop of plasma erupting from a star's surface," team member Natasha Hurley-Walker of the International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research (ICRAR), Curtin University, Australia, said. "It's amazing that by using radio wavelengths we can detect the storms on a star over 5,000 light-years away." South Africa’s MeerKAT telescope. (Image credit: South African Radio Astronomy Observatory (SARAO)) Hurley-Walker and the team at ICRAR have been at the cutting edge of rare star systems like this. "We detected this system in a large survey using the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA) to scan the entire Milky Way visible from Australia," Hurley-Walker said. "We then used the MeerKAT radio telescope in South Africa to determine its precise position." After the radio telescopes detected this LPT, it was confirmed using the W.M. Keck Observatory on Maunakea in Hawaii. The visible light follow-up of Keck also confirmed that the star in GPM J071507−114153 was a G-type star, just like the sun. science.title: Gemini Astronaut Photos Inspired Early Earth Observation Program
science.description: NASA astronauts James A. Lovell Jr. and Edwin E. “Buzz” Aldrin Jr. captured this image of the area surrounding the Red Sea and Nile river valley on November 14, 1966, during their four-day mission in space. Gemini XII was the final flight of NASA’s Gemini Program. NASA Astronauts James A. Lovell Jr. and Edwin E. “Buzz” Aldrin Jr. orbited Earth from November 11 to 15, 1966, on Gemini XII , the final mission of NASA’s Gemini program. In addition to successfully completing rendezvous maneuvers and spacewalks, procedures vital to sending American astronauts to the Moon, the crew was also spurring the development of a different field of exploration, observing Earth from space. The photos taken by Lovell, Aldrin, and other Gemini astronauts demonstrated the value of orbital imagery for studying Earth’s surface. Their images helped scientists make the case for a dedicated Earth observation satellite program. One of strongest advocates for accelerating the use of Earth-observing satellites was William T. Pecora, the director of the United States Geological Survey from 1965 to 1971. In a 1969 statement, Pecora noted that the Earth Resources Observation Satellite (EROS) program he championed, and which later paved the way for Landsat , was “conceived in 1966 largely as a direct result of the demonstrated utility of Mercury and Gemini orbital photography to Earth resource studies.” For more than five decades, Landsat and other Earth-observing satellites have provided invaluable data used around the world to monitor crops, wildfires, flooding, vegetation health, land use, and countless other changes to our planet.
